component_findings.current_knowledge: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--go): Multiple widely-cited published books and an active weekly-format podcast (Go Time) plus a long-running historical talks/presentations archive (talks.golang.org, A Tour of Go, Getting Started with Go) demonstrate durable, non-ephemeral public learning material beyond forum posts.
component_findings.events_groups: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--go): The community-maintained Go Wiki catalogs user groups and meetups across many cities, a diversity-focused outreach group (GoBridge), an independent Discourse forum, a comprehensive conference list, and a companies-using-Go registry.
component_findings.international_breadth: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--go): Go has one of the denser annual global conference circuits observed among mainstream languages in this batch: a US flagship (GopherCon, described by aggregators as the world's largest and longest-running Go-specific conference) plus regional editions in Europe, Africa, Singapore, China, and Israel, alongside independent events (GolangConf, GopherCamp, GoLab, Go Conference Japan, TinyGo Conf) tracked on the official community wiki.
component_findings.learning_materials: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--go): Multiple widely-cited published books and an active weekly-format podcast (Go Time) plus a long-running historical talks/presentations archive (talks.golang.org, A Tour of Go, Getting Started with Go) demonstrate durable, non-ephemeral public learning material beyond forum posts.
component_findings.qa_discussion: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--go): Go's own help page enumerates a dedicated discussion forum, live Discord support, a Slack channel, and an IRC channel, plus an FAQ, in addition to release-announcement mailing lists, an official blog, and official Bluesky/Mastodon/Twitter accounts and a monitored subreddit.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.limitations: Raw counts such as subreddit subscriber totals, Stack Overflow tag question counts, and conference attendance figures were not independently re-verified against a live API in this pass beyond secondary aggregator pages (e.g., frontpagemetrics.com, subredditstats.com), and such popularity/traffic proxies are treated per methodology as supporting context only, not as a standalone score. No non-English localized-documentation coverage was independently examined beyond the Go Wiki's own pointer to a NonEnglish page.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Inspect the same knowledge channels for every language and use current, publicly accessible evidence rather than raw search-result counts alone.

snapshot_recertification.policy: legacy evidence re-adjudicated under current runner-owned rubric
